name: jless
summary: A terminal JSON viewer for reading, exploring and searching JSON data with collapsible structure and vim-style navigation.
use_cases: view JSON files in the terminal
search JSON data with regular expressions
features: expand and collapse objects and arrays

usage_guide.open_hint: Run `jless <file>` to open a JSON file in the viewer, and press q to quit.

features.title: View JSON with syntax highlighting
steps: Run `jless <file>` to open a JSON file.
Read the colored, line-numbered tree of keys and values.

features.feature: expand and collapse objects and arrays
features.title: Expand and collapse objects and arrays
steps: Move to an object or array and press Space to collapse it into one line.
Press Space again to expand it.

features.title: Move around with vim-style keys
steps: Press j to move down one line.
Press G to jump to the last item; the status bar shows its path, such as .note.

features.title: Search JSON with regular expressions
steps: Type / followed by a regular expression and press Enter.
Press n to go to the next match; the status bar shows the match count and path.

setup.command:
cd ~/work && cat > sample.json <<'EOF'
{"name": "jules", "kind": "jellyfish", "tags": ["mascot", "logo"], "stats": {"arms": 8, "alive": true}, "note": "found in the deep sea"}
EOF
cat > drive.py <<'EOF'
import os, pty, sys, time, re, select, struct, fcntl, termios
f = sys.argv[1]; keys = sys.argv[2:]
pid, fd = pty.fork()
if pid == 0:
    os.environ['TERM'] = 'xterm-256color'
    os.execvp('jless', ['jless', f])
fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', 24, 80, 0, 0))
def read(t=1.0):
    out = b''; end = time.time() + t
    while time.time() < end:
        r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.1)
        if r:
            try: d = os.read(fd, 65536)
            except OSError: break
            if not d: break
            out += d
    return out.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
def show(label, s):
    colors = len(re.findall(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*3[0-9;]*m', s))
    txt = re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[A-Za-z]', ' ', s)
    txt = re.sub(r'\x1b[()][A-Z0-9]|\x1b[=>]', '', txt)
    txt = re.sub(r'[ \t]+', ' ', txt)
    print('=== %s (color escapes: %d) ===' % (label, colors))
    print(txt.strip())
show('initial', read(1.5))
for k in keys:
    k = k.encode().decode('unicode_escape')
    os.write(fd, k.encode()); show('after %r' % k, read(0.8))
os.write(fd, b'q'); read(0.8)
_, st = os.waitpid(pid, 0)
print('jless exit status:', os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(st))
sys.exit(os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(st))
EOF

pitfalls.readme_said: Install via cargo install jless or OS package managers (pacman, xbps, pkgin, pkg)
pitfalls.actually_needed: No Rust toolchain or root here, so I used the prebuilt release binary the README links from its releases page (v0.9.0 x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu zip)

pitfalls.readme_said: The release binary is presented as a single standalone binary; X11 libraries are mentioned only for building from source
pitfalls.actually_needed: The prebuilt Linux binary is dynamically linked against libxcb.so.1, libxcb-render.so.0, libxcb-shape.so.0 and libxcb-xfixes.so.0 and fails to start without them (libxcb1, libxcb-render0, libxcb-shape0, libxcb-xfixes0 runtime packages)

pitfalls.readme_said: sudo apt-get install the libxcb packages
pitfalls.actually_needed: Without root: download the bookworm .debs from deb.debian.org, unpack them with dpkg -x into ~/.local/xcb, and run jless through a wrapper that sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH

It needs a TTY, so the checks drove it through a Python pty script (drive.py, setup command 7) that sends keystrokes and prints the screen with ANSI codes stripped. Typed-ahead input after '/' was dropped, so the keys must be sent separately

judge.observed: The captured output shows jless rendering sample.json with name : "jules", collapsing the root to '1 ▶ (5) {name: "jules"' after a space keypress, and printing 'jless 0.9.0'; the screenshots of the first two checks show only the header and status lines, not the rendered JSON.

what_it_does.quote:
Expand and collapse objects and arrays so you can see both the high-
  and low-level structure of the data.

who_it_is_for.quote:
Use it as a
replacement for whatever combination of `less`, `jq`, `cat` and your
editor you currently use for viewing JSON files.

prerequisites.quote:
On Linux systems, X11 libraries are needed to build clipboard access if
building from source.

config_and_keys.quote: There is not yet support for a jless config file, so if you would like relative line numbers by default, it is recommended to set up an alias

license_and_platforms.quote: `jless` currently supports macOS and Linux. Windows support is planned.
